title: Duplicate: Ellington sidemen and Louis's advice

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Yeah. Was it Toby and Sonny?
And Sonny, the guitar player. And Braut on bass, of course, Duke on the piano. And we just had -- that was all, at that time.
Fred Guy, Sonny Greer, Braut on bass, Bubba and --
Tricky Sam was on trombone. Yeah.

Uh-huh. Now, we made records, started making records like that, yeah. Of course, in later years, he changed. Men died or left, like that. All the bands have to change the men, yeah, different reasons.

But, anyhow, I was telling you about going away to Europe. Well, I explained to Duke about my position. Louis Armstrong had told me, he said, Scottie, you're a city boy. You never been South, because I hadn't. He said, don't go South, because you wouldn't understand it.

He told me that. We were talking one day, like fellows do, just -- he said, don't go South because you wouldn't understand it. Well, to this day, I haven't been any further South than Richmond, Virginia. Because when I went to California, I went by the Northern route, around Cleveland and Chicago and all like that way. I haven't been South.
